$comment: Mach-O EXECUTABLE (MH_EXECUTE) for x86_64 Darwin/macOS. Second Mach-O schema (plan 14 LK3 cycle 2, 2026-05-30). Consumed by `src/link/format/macho.cpp` via the format-blind linker engine. Differs from `macho64-x86_64-darwin.format.json` (the MH_OBJECT schema) in: `macho.filetype = 2` (MH_EXECUTE); `macho.flags` includes MH_PIE (0x200000) + MH_NOUNDEFS (0x1) + MH_DYLDLINK (0x4) + MH_TWOLEVEL (0x80) = 0x200085 (modern macOS exec convention); sections carry `virtualAddress` (loaded at ImageBase + offset); top-level `entryPoint` names the LC_MAIN entry-function symbol; new `image` block carries __PAGEZERO size + LC_LOAD_DYLINKER path + LC_LOAD_DYLIB list.
$stackReserveUnsupportedReasonComment: D-SQLITE-PE64-FULL-TIER-STACK-DEPTH: Mach-O CAN express a per-program stack reserve -- `LC_MAIN.stacksize` is a genuine equivalent of the PE optional header's SizeOfStackReserve -- but NO DSS walker arm writes it yet, so this schema deliberately declares no `stackReserveControl` and a request is REFUSED. Shipping the capability without the walker would let a request be accepted and silently dropped; declaring the gap keeps it VISIBLE. TRACKED as [[D-LK-MACHO-STACK-RESERVE-LC-MAIN]] -- and that registry row is the point: unlike the other three reason verbs (`runtime-controlled`, `loader-ignores-field`, `no-image-field`), which state PERMANENT facts about a platform, this one names a gap that is OURS and is CLOSABLE, so it carries a trigger and defined closing work in the backlog rather than only a well-written comment (the comment tells whoever HITS it; the row is what keeps it from being forgotten). When the macho walker arm lands, this key is replaced by a `stackReserveControl` block with a `macho-lc-main` vehicle and this format moves to the positive side of the linker gate's coverage sweep.
$dataModelComment: FC3 c1: 64-bit linux/darwin are LP64 (int 32, long 64, ptr 64). Consumed by the semantic tier (buildCuMir threads format.dataModel() into analyze()): c-subset long binds I64 here. REQUIRED closed-enum field; the loader rejects a missing or unknown value (a silent default would bake wrong widths).
$headerNameMatchingComment: D-PP-HEADER-CASE-INSENSITIVE-PE: macOS ships on APFS/HFS+ volumes that are CASE-INSENSITIVE by default (the installer default since 10.13; a case-sensitive volume is opt-in), and Apple's own SDK headers rely on it -- `<TargetConditionals.h>` / `<CoreFoundation/CoreFoundation.h>` are routinely spelled with divergent case. REQUIRED closed-enum field. DSS ASCII-folds the comparison ITSELF per path component rather than delegating to fs::exists, so a Darwin cross-build from a case-sensitive Linux host resolves exactly as it does natively.
$predefinedMacrosComment: TF-C97 (D-PP-FORMAT-DATA-MODEL-PREDEFINES): the C-visible face of this file's `dataModel` above, DERIVED FROM THAT VALUE AND NEVER FROM THIS FILE'S NAME -- the loader synthesizes no macro name and the engine performs no format-identity branch; it merges whatever rows are declared here with the language's `preprocess.predefinedMacros` and the target's `predefinedMacros`, applying `availableObjectFormats` exactly once. DECLARED ON THE FORMAT because the data model is per-(OS x format), not per-CPU: the same x86_64 target is LP64 here and LLP64 under pe64-x86_64-windows-*, so a target-side row would be wrong on one of its own formats -- which is exactly what both .target.json files say when they record `__LP64__`/`_LP64` as DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED and defer to the format. BOTH spellings, each value 1: MEASURED 2026-07-30 with `/usr/bin/clang -dM -E -x c /dev/null -target <triple>` (Apple clang 21.0.0), __LP64__ and _LP64 are BOTH defined as 1 on arm64-apple-darwin, x86_64-apple-darwin, aarch64-linux-gnu and x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, and NEITHER is defined on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc. COLLISION POLICY: a name declared by this file AND the language or target config is FATAL (C_ConflictingPredefinedMacro) -- no side silently wins. WHAT IT UNBLOCKS, MEASURED: the macOS SDK gates 234 occurrences across 91 headers on __LP64__, so without these rows DSS compiled the SDK's ILP32 arms while its own widths were LP64 (sizeof(long)==8), and $SDK/usr/include/mach/port.h:113-114 then asserted the user32 struct size 12 instead of user64's 16 -- sqlite mem1.c's three error[S0029]. RED-ON-DISABLE: delete this key and examples/c-subset/predefined_lp64_macho stops exiting 42.
$bitFieldStrategyComment: D-CSUBSET-BITFIELD-ABI-EXACT: macOS x86_64 generic LSB-first bit-field allocation == gnu_packed (Apple does not diverge from generic AAPCS64 on bit-field packing). Byte-ABI-exact to clang. See macho64-x86_64-darwin for the divergence-list rationale.
$longDoubleFormatComment: FC17.9(e) D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE: macOS x86_64 `long double` is the x87 80-bit extended format stored 16/16 (the SysV-x86_64 rule; Apple's x86_64 ABI follows SysV here). The axis resolves the c-subset row to F80 — declarations/layout/sizeof work; VALUE arithmetic walls loud until D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE-X87-ARITH lands.
$entryPointComment: Empty defaults to module.functions[0] (cycle-2 convention). LC_MAIN.entryoff is computed as (entry_function_offset_in_.text) — relative to the __TEXT segment start, NOT to file offset.
$externCallDispatchComment: DIRECT-PLT (corrected from the original mislabel). Mach-O resolves imports through a per-extern __stubs entry: the linker points each extern symbol's VA at its __stubs STUB (code) — see `symbolVa[extern] = stubVa` in macho.cpp — and the stub does the __got indirection internally (x86_64 `FF 25 disp32` jmp through the __got slot; ARM64 ADRP+LDR+BR x16). The call site is therefore a PLAIN DIRECT call (x86_64 `E8 disp32`, ARM64 `BL`) to the stub — byte-identical in shape to an intra-module call — NOT an `FF 15`-through-the-stub deref (that would dereference the stub's CODE bytes as a function pointer → SIGSEGV). This is the SAME direct-plt model ELF uses, and it matches what the trampoline + MIR→LIR `lowerCall` emit. D-FFI-EXTERN-CALL-DISPATCH.
$entryClusterDischargedComment: ★ THE D-LK10-ENTRY-MACHO-EXIT DEFERRAL IS DISCHARGED HERE — this key pair REPLACES the `$processExitDeferredComment` that stood in this slot. That comment posed the choice as (a) by-name-import of libSystem `_exit` vs (b) the raw BSD syscall 0x2000001, deferred the answer 'to the first Mach-O runnable-binary trigger', and closed by calling the resulting silent skip 'intentional, not a defect'. BOTH halves are now obsolete. THE CHOICE WAS MADE AND SHIPPED: the arm64 sibling took option (a) and is the RUNTIME-WITNESSED leg (a DSS-built mach-o exec ran on the operator's Apple Silicon Mac); Apple declares BSD syscall numbers unstable across macOS versions, and libSystem is loaded by every macOS process anyway, which is what settled (a) over (b). ★ SAY THE EVIDENCE GRADE PLAINLY, BECAUSE THIS FILE HOLDS ITSELF TO A STRICTER ONE TWELVE LINES DOWN. The runtime witness is arm64's; there is NO x86_64 macOS witness in this project (the operator's Mac is Apple Silicon), so the entry cluster shipped HERE is INFERRED, not measured: `_exit` is the same libSystem symbol under the same format-kind mangling rule, and `sysv_amd64` derives from the abi_catalog x86_64+MachO row plus the same-named convention on x86_64.target.json. An earlier wording said 'the trigger the deferral waited for has already fired for this format family', which reads as though the x86_64 cluster inherited the arm64 run — it did not. What actually forces the cluster to ship regardless is the new validate() rule: an MH_EXECUTE schema declaring no `processExit` is now rejected at config load, so 'omit until witnessed' (the stance `$remainingDeliberateOmissionsComment` still takes for the data sections) is not an available option here. Ship it INFERRED and say so, rather than let two evidentiary standards sit unremarked in one file. AND THE SILENT SKIP IS NO LONGER THE PROJECT'S POSITION: `format.processExit().has_value()` returning false on an EXEC-flavored format means the emitted image's entry points straight at the user's `main` with no exit spine — a program that falls off the end of `main` into whatever follows it, produced with NO diagnostic. That is a silent-miscompile shape, and this cycle makes it fail LOUD instead. A format that claims MH_EXECUTE must therefore declare its exit spine; this file now does. NOTE the deliberate NON-symmetry with the arm64 sibling: only the ENTRY CLUSTER is being brought over. Everything else this file omits stays omitted on purpose — see $remainingDeliberateOmissionsComment below, which names the test that pins each one.
$processExitComment: STDIO-FLUSH-AT-EXIT / D-LK10-ENTRY-MACHO-EXIT: the macOS runnable-binary exit terminates via the C-standard `exit(3)` — which flushes line-/full-buffered stdio + runs `atexit` handlers before the process dies (returning from `main` is equivalent to calling `exit(3)`). importMangledName `_exit` is the MACH-O SYMBOL for the C function `exit`, NOT the non-flushing POSIX `_exit(2)`: Apple's C ABI prefixes every C symbol with ONE leading underscore, and that rule is keyed on the FORMAT KIND rather than the CPU (cFormatAddsLeadingUnderscore(MachO)=true; applyCMangling("exit",MachO)="_exit"), so the x86_64 slice of libSystem exports the flushing `exit(3)` under exactly the name the arm64 slice does. (The POSIX `_exit(2)` is a DIFFERENT symbol, `__exit` — two underscores.) importLibraryPath is the SAME `/usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib` as the arm64 sibling and that is not a copied arch claim: the dylib is UNIVERSAL, and which slice of it this image binds against is decided by `macho.cputype` below. The trampoline places the name VERBATIM into the synthetic ExternImport (entry_trampoline.cpp does not re-mangle a processExit import), moves the user fn's return value (sysv_amd64 returnGprs[0]=rax) into argGprs[0]=rdi — a REAL `mov` here, UNLIKE the arm64 arm where the same step is a no-op x0->x0 emitted only for ABI uniformity — then makes a DIRECT call to the `_exit` __stubs entry (externCallDispatch=direct-plt above; the x86_64 stub is the 6-byte `FF 25 disp32` jmp through its __got slot, `emitX86_64MachoStub` at src/link/format/macho.cpp:301). importLibraryPath must also appear in image.loadDylibs so dyld can resolve it — it already does. Uniform with elf (libc `exit`) + pe (kernel32 `ExitProcess`, msvcrt DLL-detach flush): all four exec formats terminate through a stdio-flushing libc-level primitive.
$entryCallingConventionComment: sysv_amd64 — ★ MEASURED, and deliberately NOT the arm64 sibling's `apple_arm64`. A verbatim clone of that value is the obvious mistake here and it would fail loud in `injectEntryTrampoline`'s `target.callingConventionByName(ccName)` lookup (src/link/entry_trampoline.cpp — cited BY CONSTRUCT because the line range this comment originally carried had already drifted by the end of the cycle that wrote it), which resolves this string against the TARGET's callingConventions and reports when the name does not exist. THE EVIDENCE, three independent in-tree sites that agree: (1) the ABI catalog pins the row `{ "x86_64", ObjectFormatKind::MachO, CallConv::CcSysV, "sysv_amd64" }` at src/ffi/abi/abi_catalog.cpp:55 — the same file gives arm64+MachO its own `apple_arm64` row at :58, so the two verbs are per-CPU and not interchangeable; (2) src/dss-config/targets/x86_64.target.json:2338 ships a calling convention of exactly this name (SysV AMD64: int args RDI/RSI/RDX/RCX/R8/R9, int return RAX); (3) tests/mir/test_mir_lowering_c_subset.cpp:1127 already pairs `macho64-x86_64-darwin-exec` with `sysv_amd64` in its shipped-row table. Apple's x86_64 ABI IS System V AMD64 — the divergence list that earns arm64 a separate verb (always-stack varargs, indirect-result) has no x86_64 counterpart, so there is no `apple_x86_64` to declare and none was invented. Read via `target.callingConventionByName("sysv_amd64")` at trampoline-build time; the scalar exit call exercises neither the red zone nor the stack-argument rules. Same verb the elf64-x86_64-linux-exec sibling declares — the CPU fixes it, and Linux and Darwin agree because SysV is the ABI on both.
$remainingDeliberateOmissionsComment: ★ WHAT THIS FILE STILL DOES NOT DECLARE, AND WHY EACH ABSENCE IS DELIBERATE RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT. Written down because the arm64 sibling HAS all of these, which makes the gap look like an unfinished copy — it is not, and a well-meaning 'complete it from the sibling' edit turns four separate tests RED. ★ EVERY ROW BELOW CITES ITS PINNING TEST BY NAME, NOT BY LINE RANGE, AND THAT IS A CORRECTION: the ranges this block originally carried were read on 2026-08-05 and THREE of the six had already drifted before the same cycle ended — one of them onto a test asserting the OPPOSITE of the row it was cited for. The TEST NAMES below were re-verified by reading each test on 2026-08-05; a name survives an edit above it, a line number does not. (1) `supportedDataSections` + the `tdata`/`tbss` kinds + `tlsAccess` — PINNED by tests/link/test_linker.cpp `Linker.TdataItemOnNonOptedInFormatsRejectsAtAcceptsGate`, which asserts ASSERT_FALSE(acceptsDataSection(Tdata)) and the same for Tbss on this exact format name, with the message 'must not opt into tdata before its TLS cycle lands'. (2) a `rodata` row in `sections[]` (`__TEXT,__const`) — PINNED by tests/asm/test_asm_substrate.cpp `AsmSubstrate.ShippedExecFormatsRodataSectionPerWalkerArm`, EXPECT_EQ(sectionByKind(Rodata), nullptr), whose own comment says the Mach-O walker arm is anchored OPEN at D-LK3-RODATA and instructs the reader to 'flip this EQ to NE' only in the SAME slice that closes it. The `data`/`bss`/`tdata`/`tbss`/`tvars` rows ride the same decision. (3) `image.segmentPageSize` — its ABSENCE is the point: tests/link/test_macho_arm64_exit.cpp `MachOArm64Exit.X86DarwinExecDefaultsTo4KSegmentPageSize` is an explicit knob-that-lies guard proving the absent-key path defaults to 4096 (the `kDefaultMachoSegmentPageSize` constant in src/link/object_format_schema.hpp), which is the CORRECT x86_64 macOS VM page where Apple Silicon needs 16384. Declaring 16384 here would be doubly wrong — it also breaks validate()'s Mach-O mmap-congruence rule (the `not aligned to segmentPageSize` failure in src/link/object_format_schema.cpp), since this file's __text virtualAddress 0x100001000 is 0x1000 above pageZeroSize and therefore congruent under a 4 KiB page and NOT under a 16 KiB one. (4) `image.buildVersion` — PINNED by the SAME test as (3), `MachOArm64Exit.X86DarwinExecDefaultsTo4KSegmentPageSize`, whose second assertion is EXPECT_FALSE(buildVersion.has_value()), commented 'x86 declares no buildVersion (Intel/Rosetta is lenient)'. (One test, two rows — the old two separate line ranges implied two tests and there was only ever one.) (5) `image.codeSignature` — PINNED by tests/link/test_codesign_placeholder.cpp `MachOCodeSignPlaceholder.ZeroSizeOmitsLcCodeSignature`, which asserts codeSignatureSize == 0 on this format AND walks the emitted load commands asserting LC_CODE_SIGNATURE (0x1D) is never emitted; DOCUMENTED that mandatory code signing is an Apple-Silicon kernel rule, not an x86_64 one, so the absence costs nothing on this slice. (★ do NOT re-cite this by line: the range this row used to carry now lands inside `DynamicPathEmitsLcCodeSignatureWithZeroReservation`, which asserts the OPPOSITE.) (6) `processArgs` — PINNED by tests/link/test_object_format_schema.cpp `ProcessArgsSubstrate.ShippedMachoExecsDeclareNoneAndPeDeclaresCrtOutParam` for BOTH darwin execs, and CORRECT on the merits: dyld calls an LC_MAIN entry with argc/argv ALREADY in the argument registers, so pass-through IS the mechanism and a stack-vector block would read a stack that holds no argv there. (7) `dataImportBinding` / `artifactProfiles` / `librarySynthesis` — no test pins these, and they are simply not this cycle's scope; each fails LOUD rather than silently when reached (MEASURED 2026-08-05: a TU with `#include <stdio.h>` + printf walls at `error[K_FormatLacksImportSupport] ... extern DATA import '___stdinp' ... declares no 'dataImportBinding' model`, and one with `const char msg[]="hello"` walls at `error[K_NoMatchingObjectFormat] ... section=rodata ... does not advertise that section`). ★ ONE CORRECTION FOR WHOEVER CLOSES THESE, because the reason matters: the blocker is NOT missing walker code. MEASURED 2026-08-05 by declaring the full sibling key set in a THROWAWAY copy of this file and emitting real binaries — the format-blind macho walker produced correct x86_64 images with `__TEXT,__const`, `__DATA,__data`, `__DATA,__bss`, the three S_THREAD_LOCAL_* TLV sections, a `__got` slot bound for the `___stdinp` data import, 4 KiB-strided segments and 6-byte stubs, all rc=0. So these are POLICY deferrals awaiting a macOS-x86_64 RUNTIME WITNESS (this project has none — the operator's Mac is Apple Silicon) plus the anchored walker-arm review, NOT unwritten code. That probe was reverted; nothing of it ships.

macho.$comment: mach_header_64 identity. cputype = CPU_TYPE_X86_64 (0x01000007). cpusubtype = CPU_SUBTYPE_X86_64_ALL (3). filetype = 'execute' (MH_EXECUTE, closed enum). flags = MH_NOUNDEFS (0x1) | MH_DYLDLINK (0x4) | MH_TWOLEVEL (0x80) | MH_PIE (0x200000) = 0x200085 — modern macOS exec convention: no unresolved symbols at link time, uses dyld, two-level namespace lookup, position-independent.

image.$comment: Mach-O image fields for MH_EXECUTE. pageZeroSize = 0x100000000 (4 GiB) — the __PAGEZERO segment placed at vmaddr=0 catches null-pointer derefs at the kernel level. dylinkerPath = '/usr/lib/dyld' — the dynamic linker macOS always uses. loadDylibs = ['/usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib'] — required for any user-space process (provides start function + libc + Mach traps). Future cycles add Foundation / AppKit / etc. as needed.
image.$bindNowComment: Eager binding — the v1 stance per plan 14 §5 risk row, parallel to ELF cycle 2b.2's DF_1_NOW choice. Emits LC_DYLD_INFO_ONLY with the immediate bind_off opcode stream resolved at load via the linker; lazy_bind_off stays zero. Lazy upgrade (lazy_bind opcode stream resolved on first call via dyld_stub_binder) anchored at D-LK6-13; until then, the walker fails loud on bindNow=false.

sections.$comment: __text within __TEXT segment. virtualAddress = 0x100000000 + 0x1000 = 0x100001000 — __TEXT loads immediately after __PAGEZERO at the page boundary. flags (in substrate `type` field) = S_REGULAR (0) | S_ATTR_PURE_INSTRUCTIONS (0x80000000) | S_ATTR_SOME_INSTRUCTIONS (0x00000400) = 0x80000400. addrAlign = 16 (x86_64 instruction alignment).
sections.name: __text

relocations.$comment: Mach-O image-side relocs reuse the same kinds as the .o schema (BRANCH/UNSIGNED_8/UNSIGNED_4). cycle-2 walker applies intra-module relocs in-place via the LK6 cycle 1 structured-formula triple; the relocation_info records are NOT emitted for MH_EXECUTE (dyld doesn't read .o-style relocs — it reads LC_DYLD_INFO chained-fixups, which arrive at LK6 cycle 2 paired with FFI). nativeId packs (type<<28)|(length<<25)|(pcrel<<24) — same as the .o schema. r_extern (bit 27) + r_symbolnum (bits 0..23) are walker-filled.
relocations.name: X86_64_RELOC_BRANCH
